spec.description: Each running Flowrensic server, called an instance here, and what it uses and logs. Each line is one instance, named by the address Prometheus reads its metrics at. The CPU and memory of the whole container against its limits are on the sustainability dashboard. The whole section has no data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the servers.

options.content:
## Instances
The running Flowrensic instances, and what each one uses and logs.

spec.title: Running instances
spec.description: One row for each Flowrensic server that Prometheus scrapes: its address, its host name, up, the CPU cores it uses, its memory in bytes, Go processors, how many threads may run Go code at once, and GOGC, the garbage collection setting, 100 by default. Up comes from Prometheus: 1 when the server answered the last scrape, 0 when it did not. Normal: every server you run, with up 1. Bad: up 0, the server is down or cannot be reached; its host name stays for an hour. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers under the job name flowrensic, for example when the metrics are only pushed over OTLP.

spec.title: CPU load by instance
spec.description: CPU cores each server process uses: 1 is one full core. It counts the Flowrensic process only, not Postgres or other containers. Normal: low, with short peaks while it pulls or judges runs. Bad: it stays close to the cores the server has; see the CPU against the limit on the sustainability dashboard. No data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server.

spec.title: Memory used against the memory limit by instance
spec.description: Memory the Go runtime of each server holds, in bytes, against two limits: the Go limit, GOMEMLIMIT, and the memory limit of the container. Normal: up and down around a steady level, well under the limits. Bad: it keeps climbing and does not come back down, a leak, or it comes close to a limit; at the container limit the server is killed. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the server under the job name flowrensic, since the Go numbers are read with that job name. No Go limit line when GOMEMLIMIT is not set, and no container line when the server runs with no memory limit.

spec.title: Network data volume per second by instance (total)
spec.description: Bytes per second each server read and wrote on its main listener together: the API, the UI and the history downloads. The metrics endpoint is not counted. There is no good or bad value of its own; it follows the requests. A jump with no more requests means larger requests or answers. No data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server, or before the first request.

spec.title: Network data volume per second by instance (in / out)
spec.description: The same bytes as the panel on the left, split in two lines: bytes read in requests and bytes written in answers, per second. Normal: most data comes in from the workers and goes out to the UI. Bad: a line that keeps climbing with no more requests. No data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server, or before the first request.

spec.title: Requests per second to instance
spec.description: HTTP requests each server answered per second on its main listener, whatever the answer: the API, the UI and the history downloads. There is no good or bad value of its own; a drop to 0 while workers run means they stopped sending. No data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server, or before the first request.

spec.title: Response latency p50, p95, p99 by instance
spec.description: Three lines, p50, p95 and p99: the time in seconds in which half, 95% and 99% of the API calls of each server were answered, over the last few minutes. It counts the calls of the API only, not the pages of the UI or the history downloads. Normal: well under 1 second, the request time limit by default; the limit is drawn for each kind of request on the sustainability dashboard. Bad: a line that climbs or stays high. No data when there was no API call in that time.

spec.title: Errors per second by instance
spec.description: Log lines at level error that each server wrote per second. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, something failed; read the log of that server for the error. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: Warns per second by instance
spec.description: Log lines at level warn that each server wrote per second. Normal: 0 or a few now and then, for example when an engine could not be reached once. Bad: a steady or growing line; read the log of that server. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server.

spec.title: Goroutines leak detector by instance
spec.description: How many goroutines each server runs, a count. A goroutine is a light thread of the Go runtime. Normal: up and down around a steady level as work comes and goes. Bad: a line that keeps climbing and does not come back down, a leak. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the server under the job name flowrensic, since the Go numbers are read with that job name.

How much the database and the blob storage hold, and what retention deleted. The database is Postgres. The blob storage is where the history files are kept: a folder, a MinIO bucket or an S3 bucket. Each panel is one value for the whole install, so several servers on one database show the same number. The whole section has no data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the servers.

options.content:
## Storage
The database on the left and the blob storage on the right.

spec.title: Database storage used volume
spec.description: Size of the Postgres database, in bytes, as Postgres reports it. Normal: it grows with use and levels off once retention deletes old data. Bad: it keeps growing toward the store size limit, 10 GB by default for the database and the history files together; the sustainability dashboard draws that limit. No data when the server could not read the size, which it logs as a warning.

spec.title: Blob storage used volume
spec.description: Size of the history files or objects, in bytes, from the note the database keeps of each file, so the bucket is not listed. Normal: it grows with use and levels off once retention deletes old runs. Bad: it keeps growing toward the store size limit, which counts the database and the history files together. No data when the server could not read the size, which it logs as a warning.

spec.title: Database storage total records
spec.description: Rows in the database, a count: runs, findings, activity attempts and engine samples together. There is no good or bad value of its own; it follows use. Bad: it keeps growing and never levels off, so retention may not keep up. No data when the server could not read the counts, which it logs as a warning.

spec.title: Blob storage used total items
spec.description: History files or objects the blob storage holds, a count, about one for each stored run. There is no good or bad value of its own; it follows the runs stored. Bad: it keeps growing and never levels off, so retention may not keep up. No data when the server could not read the count, which it logs as a warning.

spec.title: Database evicted items
spec.description: Rows retention deleted from the database in the time range shown, a count, of every kind, for their age or for the size limit. Normal: some, once data reaches its age limit. Bad: a jump, the size limit made retention delete data early; the server logs a warning for each such deletion. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: Blob evicted items
spec.description: History objects retention deleted in the time range shown, a count, one for each run it deleted. Normal: some, once runs reach their age limit. Bad: a jump, the size limit made retention delete runs early. No data or 0 until retention deleted its first run.

spec.title: Ephemeral run clocks by instance
spec.description: How many ephemeral runs the clock of each server holds an entry for, a count. Normal: up and down with the ephemeral runs in flight. Bad: a line that keeps climbing and does not come back down, entries that are never let go. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers.

spec.title: Memory allocated per second by instance
spec.description: Bytes the Go runtime of each server allocates on the heap per second. Normal: it follows the load. Bad: it climbs while the load does not, more garbage for the collector. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the server under the job name flowrensic, since the Go numbers are read with that job name.

spec.title: Allocations per second by instance
spec.description: Heap allocations the Go runtime of each server makes per second, a count. Normal: it follows the load. Bad: it climbs while the load does not. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the server under the job name flowrensic, since the Go numbers are read with that job name.

spec.title: Garbage collections per second by instance
spec.description: How many times per second the Go runtime of each server collected garbage. Normal: a few a second or less. Bad: many a second, the server spends its CPU on collecting; look at the memory allocated. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers.

spec.title: Heap goal by instance
spec.description: The heap size in bytes at which the Go runtime of each server starts its next garbage collection. Normal: steady, above the memory in use. Bad: close to the memory limit. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the server under the job name flowrensic, since the Go numbers are read with that job name.

spec.title: History files read per second
spec.description: History files read from the blob storage per second: one line for each call that asked for them, background for the jobs, and one line for the analysis. Normal: low, a list or a count never reads a history file. Bad: a line for a list call, or reads that climb with the stored data. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers.

spec.title: History bytes written per second
spec.description: Bytes of history written to the blob storage per second, before compression. Normal: it follows the runs that close. Bad: 0 while runs close, or far above History bytes per second on the storage and ingest dashboard. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers.

The queries the servers send to the database. Each query is named by the name of the query, or by the Go function that runs it when it has none. The whole section has no data when Prometheus gets no metrics from the servers.

options.content:
## Database
How long the queries of the servers take, and how often a query waits for a connection.

spec.title: Query time p50, p95, p99
spec.description: Three lines, p50, p95 and p99: the time in seconds in which half, 95% and 99% of all queries finished, over the last few minutes, all servers together. Normal: p95 well under 0.1 seconds. Bad: p95 or p99 near a second, the screens and the jobs slow down; the ten slowest queries say which. No data while no query ran in that time.

spec.title: Queries per second by query name
spec.description: Queries per second of each name, all servers together. Normal: steady for each name. Bad: a name that climbs with the stored data and not with the load. No data while no query ran in that time.

spec.title: Ten slowest queries by p95
spec.description: The ten queries with the highest p95 over the selected period, with their p50, p95 and p99 in seconds. Normal: all under 0.1 seconds. Bad: a query near a second or over it; it is the first one to look at. No data while no query ran in the period.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))) and on(query) topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))) and on(query) topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))) and on(query) topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query) (rate(flowrensic_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[$__range]))))

spec.title: Waits for a database connection per second by pool
spec.description: Times per second a query waited for a free connection of the pool of its server, by pool, all servers together. Normal: 0 or near it. Bad: often above 0, the pool is too small for the work; the time waited is on the sustainability dashboard. No data when Prometheus does not scrape the servers.
